title: Exoplanet Discovery Explorer
tagline: Query the NASA Exoplanet Archive live and see how each discovery method shapes the catalog.
question: How have exoplanet discoveries changed over time, and what does each detection method let us see?
audience: Students who like space and want to learn why a catalog is not a census.

source.name: Planetary Systems Composite Parameters (pscomppars)
source.license: NASA open data; cite the dataset DOI and acknowledge the archive
source.citation: NASA Exoplanet Archive (2026), Planetary Systems Composite Parameters, NExScI-Caltech/IPAC, doi:10.26133/NEA13 (record your access date)

lesson.title: A catalog is not a census
lesson.summary: Transits find big planets on short orbits, radial velocity finds massive ones, imaging finds young giants far out. Filtering to planets with a radius quietly removes most radial-velocity discoveries, so report missingness on the full catalog before you plot.

challenges.title: Habitable-zone shortlist
challenges.description: Add pl_eqt and st_teff to the query and filter to Earth-sized planets with equilibrium temperature 180-310 K.
challenges.outcome: A table and chart of candidates with a sentence on bias.

challenges.title: Mass-radius relation
challenges.description: Fit log(mass) vs. log(radius) for planets with both values.
challenges.outcome: Slope with a confidence interval, split at 1.5 Earth radii.

challenges.title: Facility timeline
challenges.outcome: A chart showing Kepler, K2 and TESS eras.
